segments.topic: the jump in qubits IBM's quantum computers can hold
segments.say: IBM's first public quantum computer in 2016 had just 5 qubits. By 2023 its Condor chip hit 1,121 qubits -- over 200 times more.

segments.topic: why each qubit doubles a quantum computer's power
segments.say: Here's why that number matters so much: every extra qubit doubles what's representable. Just 20 of them already pass 1,048,576 possible states at once.

segments.topic: which company's quantum chip has the most qubits
segments.say: IBM's Condor chip has 1,121 qubits. Google's newest chip, Willow, has 105 -- by that one measure, IBM is the current leader.

judge.one_line: Mostly a chart deck: bubbles, bars, a seesaw that hardly tips for a million-to-two gap, and a closing that is two numbers overlapping their labels, with Data a bystander throughout.
problems: seg4: '1.12K' is drawn over 'IBM (Condor)', and the closing is a bare two-number card with two identical Datas.
seg1: the eagle clip-art on the Eagle row is a literal pun on the chip name and covers the label.
seg1:end: the '4 times over' 2x2 grid is a weak picture of 4x, and Data stands on a ladder beside it doing nothing.
seg2: the seesaw tilts only gently for 1,048,576 vs 2, and Data is cut off at the left edge and covers the '1' of 1,048,576.
Hook/seg0: it opens on an already-built bubble chart with the voice line 'this number just broke every chart', which is not much reason to stay.
Data never causes any motion: he cheers, stands, or rides in every scene.
fixes: Rebuild the closing as a physical comparison Data performs, such as stacking qubit tiles into towers of 1,121 vs 105. Measure the label and value widths so they cannot overlap.
Remove the eagle icon from the bar row.
Make the doubling literal: Data adds one qubit at a time and the pile of possible states doubles each time. The seesaw arm should slam to its stop for 1M vs 2.
Keep Data and every number fully inside the frame and off the labels.
Open on motion: for example, a 5-qubit chip that explodes into 1,121 as Data flips a switch.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.
